derived_results.claim: For each of the two four-corner variance levels sigma in {ell,u}, the equal +/-h endpoint-mean mixture is uniformly bounded by exp[-m h^2/(2 sigma^2)] times the likelihood profiled over mean at that same sigma. The proof is analytic in block mean and uses m h^2/ell^2=0.4103104144 < (2/3)log2. Combining the two variance levels gives p_rho0 <= 0.83311107702299158 p_max for every possible 32-sample block.

With the already-safe r102 scale M=1.0233202045727378, M*p_rho0 <= 0.85253939777098174 p_max. Hence q/(M p_rho0) >= 1.1729663199314464 q/p_max for every block, a uniform gain of at least 0.15953585649820393 nat/block over r85 UI. Because the delayed-start recursion is monotone in the common block multiplier, the full retained 0.25/0.25/0.50 portfolio can never alarm later on any common trajectory when UI is replaced by the scaled factor.

A new 110,000 paired path-scenario stress across two independent 11-direction exact-KL=1 Gaussian grids, two transformed reference endpoints, five changepoint ages and 500 paths per cell found scaled/UI alarm ordering 7262 earlier / 102738 equal / 0 later. Every path detected within 2048 raw post samples. When the scaled version was earlier, median reduction was 32 raw samples, mean 27.50 and maximum 64. Worst-scenario q90 envelopes (UI/scaled) over the two grids were 64/48, 64/64, 96/72, 96/96 and 128/96 for prechange ages 0,1024,10240,98304,1e6. This experiment quantifies gain only; the no-later result is already analytic.
